children: Mortgage rates rose to their highest level in over a year as tremors in the bond market threatened to push up borrowing costs for consumers.

The 30-year fixed rate averaged 6.71% this week, up from 6.66% the week prior, according to Freddie Mac. That is up from 6.23% in April, as the lack of resolution to the conflict with Iran has fueled expectations that inflation might remain stubborn.

Mortgage rates are closely tied to the 10-year Treasury yield, which earlier this week hit its highest level in almost three years as bond investors around the globe grew nervous about elevated fuel prices and soaring government deficits.

The run-up in mortgage rates is more bad news for a housing market that is now well into its fourth year of stagnation. Housing economists expect rates to remain elevated for the foreseeable future, and with inventory still limited, affordability is unlikely to improve substantially.
